transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump leaves today for a trip to Asia.
On his tour, he'll meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
NPR's Jennifer Pak reports from Beijing.
China's Foreign Ministry says the trilateral meeting is of groundbreaking significance.
It's the first meeting among China, U.S. and Russia's heads of states, according to
spokesperson Mao Ning.
She says the three leaders will talk about world peace and stability without giving details.
Trump has said he wants to negotiate a new nuclear arms control deal, while Putin is
expected to push for a peace deal over its war with Ukraine on Moscow's terms.
For China, some analysts say the meeting helps project the country and Xi as a stabilizing
force able to bring major powers together.
Jennifer Pak, NPR News, Beijing.
President Trump won't be joined on this trip by former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as
he was previously.
There's an online petition circulating calling for Huang's restoration as Nvidia chief.
Some big tech leaders have said they'll support that, including testlessly EO Elon Musk.
Musk is joining Trump on this Asia trip.
Airlines are recovering after the rare nationwide ground stop that caused chaos over the weekend.
NPR's Joel Rose reports airlines are expected to cancel fewer flights today.
Delays and disruptions continued through the weekend, as airlines scrambled to get planes
and crews back in the right places.
Airlines canceled about 2,000 flights on Sunday, according to the aviation analytics firm
Serium, or roughly 7 percent of all commercial flights.
That's high, but it is not catastrophic, and it's a big improvement from the number
of cancellations and delays on Friday and Saturday.
Airlines are hoping for something close to normal service this week, as they prepare
for the busy Thanksgiving travel season.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
A rights group says nearly 70 people in Bahrain, among them 60 Shia clerics, have been sentenced
to life in prison in a mass trial today.
And PR's Ea Batrai reports the convictions highlight how the U.S. and Israeli war on
Iran is reigniting sectarian tensions in the Gulf Arab state.
Bahrain's state news agency says the country's high criminal court found the 69 defendants
all guilty of establishing a terror group linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Bahrain says investigations found the defendants had collected funds to support Iran's Revolutionary
Guard and intended to spread a religious ideology that seeks political subordination to the
Iranian regime.
In addition to life sentences, some were also fined more than a quarter million dollars.
The Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy says several of the detained clerics had been
leading large congregations.
The rights group describes them as, quote, "casualties of the conflict" in reference
to the Iran war.
The Gulf Arab country of Bahrain is majority Shia and ruled by a Sunni monarchy with close
ties to Washington.
Aya Batrai, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR News.
The federal government will conduct a nationwide test of its emergency alert system tomorrow.
It will include TV, radio and satellite providers across the U.S. but not cell phones.
The test starts at 2.20 p.m. Eastern Time, 11.20 Pacific Time.
Regular programming will be interrupted for the test message.
No action is needed by the public.
The test is tomorrow.
The most distant human-made object ever built is set to hit a new milestone this week.
NPR's Eva Pukach reports NASA's Voyager 1 will reach one light-day distance from Earth.
A light day is the distance light travels in 24 hours.
It's equal to more than 16 billion miles from Earth.
Since launching almost 50 years ago, Voyager 1 has conducted flybys of Jupiter and Saturn
and is now charting interstellar space.
Earlier this year, NASA turned off one of its remaining science instruments to save
power and give its mission another year a breathing room.
The probe has two remaining instruments running, continuing to send data back to Earth.
To celebrate the light-day milestone, NASA is asking people to use flashlights to send
Voyager's call sign VGR in Morse code into the night sky shortly after sunset on Tuesday.
Eva Pukach and PR News.
A long-lost painting by late American artist Georgia O'Keefe will be auctioned this week.
The nearly 100-year-old painting was discovered in a New York City resident's closet.
The auction house Christie's projects it could fetch more than $3 million.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump travels to Asia to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in first trilateral summit
Airlines recover from nationwide ground stop, expecting fewer cancellations before Thanksgiving travel
Bahrain court sentences 69 defendants, including 60 Shia clerics, to life in prison
FEMA schedules nationwide emergency alert system test on TV, radio and satellite, excluding cell phones
Voyager 1 nears one light-day distance from Earth, NASA plans flashlight Morse code signal
Long-lost Georgia O'Keeffe painting found in New York closet to be auctioned this week
